title: Smallest of ten: how many looks?
hook: A tree stores the minimum of every aligned block. How many blocks cover positions 3 to 12?

knows: halving a problem and keeping a tree of results (merge-sort-payoff, heapify-from-the-bottom)
doesNotKnow: that any range query splits into a few stored nodes
that changing one value updates only the nodes on its path to the top

misconception: The minimum over positions 3 to 12 needs 10 values looked at; a stored tree cannot help with an arbitrary range.
objective: The learner can select positions 3 to 12 on a 16-position segment tree, see that it is covered by 4 stored nodes ([3], [4-7], [8-11], [12]), and explain why any range needs only about 2 log2 n nodes and an update touches log2 n + 1.

claims.text: On a tree over 16 positions, the range 3 to 12 is covered by exactly 4 stored nodes: [3], [4 to 7], [8 to 11] and [12].
claims.source: Builder's node check (2026-10-14): recursive cover (take a node wholly inside, skip one wholly outside, otherwise split into halves) returns [3,3], [4,7], [8,11], [12,12]. Demo.tsx cover() is the same rule. Matches brief cs.algorithms.md #60. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Own node re-implementation of the take/skip/split cover (fc21b/seg.mjs): [3,12] -> [3,3], [4,7], [8,11], [12,12] = 4 nodes.

claims.text: The reveal names the learner's last selected range and its node count, computed by the same take/skip/split rule (e.g. 5 to 14 needs 5), and no range of these 16 positions needs more than 6 nodes.
claims.source: Builder's node check (2026-10-14): [1,14] -> [1], [2-3], [4-7], [8-11], [12-13], [14] = 6; maximum over all 136 ranges of 16 positions is 6. Demo.tsx WIDE_COUNT and MAX_COUNT recompute both. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Own node check: [1,14] -> 6 nodes; maximum over all 136 ranges of 16 positions = 6. Matches Demo WIDE_COUNT / MAX_COUNT. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v2, wave E r6 revision by demo-builder): reveal now quotes the learner's own last range instead of 1 to 14; log2 glossed; the value change is a milestone. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own node of cover(): 5 to 14 -> [5], [6-7], [8-11], [12-13], [14] = 5; 5 to 12 -> 4; max over all 136 ranges = 6 (only 1 to 14). Reveal computes the learner's own range with the same cover().

claims.text: Every range is a union of at most about 2 log2 n stored nodes, where log2 n counts the halvings from n down to 1 (4 for 16).
claims.source: At each level of the tree the cover keeps at most two nodes (one at each ragged end), and there are log2 n + 1 levels, so at most about 2 log2 n nodes (for n = 16 the observed maximum is 6, within 2 x 4 = 8). No textbook source checked (brief lists references none); the checker should re-derive. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Re-derived and checked: at most 2 nodes taken per level (own check, n = 4..1024: max taken per level = 2); log2 n + 1 levels; observed maxima 2, 4, 6, ..., 18 = 2 log2 n - 2 for n = 4..1024, all within 2 log2 n. 'At most about' is accurate. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v2, wave E r6 revision by demo-builder): reveal now quotes the learner's own last range instead of 1 to 14; log2 glossed; the value change is a milestone. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Re-derived (pass 21 still applies): at most 2 nodes per level, log2 n + 1 levels; observed max 6 <= 8 for n = 16. Gloss 'halvings from n down to 1 (4 for 16)' is correct.

claims.text: When the learner changes one value, only the 5 nodes on its path to the top are rewritten, so both the question and the update take about log n steps.
claims.source: A position lies in exactly one node per level; 16 positions give log2 16 + 1 = 5 levels. Demo.tsx PATH_LEN counts 5 for position 9. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Own check: 31 nodes over 5 levels (16, 8, 4, 2, 1 per node); every position lies in exactly one node per level, so 5 nodes contain position 9 (Demo PATH_LEN = 5). Update rewrites those; query visits O(log n) nodes (c3). | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v2, wave E r6 revision by demo-builder): reveal now quotes the learner's own last range instead of 1 to 14; log2 glossed; the value change is a milestone. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own node: 5 blocks contain position 9 (one per level, 16/8/4/2/1); milestone changed is required, so the learner pressed the change.

claims.text: Each node stores the minimum of its positions; the tree has a node for the whole row, every aligned half, quarter, eighth and single position.
claims.source: Definition of the segment tree used here (16 = 2^4 positions, 31 nodes). The 16 stage values are hand-picked, not random; the lesson's counts do not depend on them. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Matches Demo BLOCKS: levels d = 0..4, sizes 16/2^d, aligned, 31 nodes; each displayed node value is min over its slice. Hand-picked values do not affect the counts (cover() uses only positions).

claims.text: The same tree works for maximum or sum.
claims.source: The cover and update only need an associative combine (min, max, +) for a node to be computed from its two halves. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Own randomized check: combining the cover nodes with min, max and + gives the same result as directly over the range, for all 136 ranges. Only associativity of the combine is needed.

claims.text: Once 3 to 12 is combined, the stage keeps a Seen row, '3 to 12 = [3] + [4 to 7] + [8 to 11] + [12], 4 nodes, minimum 2' (the minimum recorded at that moment), and outlines those four blocks dashed whenever they are not lit. The first 'Change the value at 9' turns 2 into 8 and the message says so ('changed from 2 to 8').
claims.source: Demo.tsx: Q_LABELS from cover(3, 12); seenMin set in combine() when lo..hi is 3..12 (START values 5 7 9 4 8 6 2 7 5 3 at 3..12, min 2); prev records vals[9] before the change (START[9] = 2, EDIT_VALUES[1] = 8). Builder revision v3 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave G r7). Builder statement, not self-verified.

recall.question: A segment tree stores the minimum of every aligned half, quarter and so on over 1,024 positions. Roughly how many stored nodes does a query for any range combine, at most?
recall.why: Only the two ragged ends need small nodes, at most two per level, and there are about log2 1,024 = 10 levels: at most about 2 x 10 = 20 nodes.
